title: Loose Belts on X or Y Axis for Hydra Series - Hydra Series
body_html:
Loose belts (X-axis or Y-axis) - Hydra Series

Problem Description

  • The starting and ending points of the cut product are misaligned or do not close accurately.
  • The edges of the lines exhibit slight waviness or vibration patterns.

Cause

The belts on the X-axis or Y-axis is either too loose or adjusted too tightly.

Solution

Important Note: 

When adjusting the belts, it is crucial to achieve a moderate tension. Belts that are either too loose or too tight on any part of the machine will negatively affect performance.

Method 1. Adjusting the Y-Axis Drive Belt

As shown in the image below, loosen the three screws in Group A to unlock the Y-axis motor bracket. Then, turn Screw B to adjust the belt tension. Once a moderate tension is achieved, re-tighten the three screws in Group A.

Method 2. Adjusting the X-Axis Drive Belt

As shown in the image below, loosen the three screws in Group A to unlock the X-axis motor bracket. Then, turn Screw B to adjust the belt tension. Once a moderate tension is achieved, re-tighten the three screws in Group A.

  • Standard Tension: When adjusting, the belt should be in a state of moderate tension. This can be assessed by the finger press test, which should allow for a slight movement margin of approximately 1 to 2 mm.
  • Over-Tension Assessment: If there is absolutely no movement when pressed, the belt is over-tightened and must be loosened slightly.

 

Final Check

  • After adjustment, manually push the laser head to slide it along the X and Y directions, observing for any sticking or abnormal noise.
  • Rerun a test job and check if the starting point and ending point misalignment issue is resolved.

 

Important Reminder:

If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
